---
title: "The Test"
---

## Format

| | Paper 1 | Paper 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Applications of Mathematical Knowledge | Mathematical Reasoning |
| Time | 75 minutes | 75 minutes |
| Questions | 20 multiple choice | 20 multiple choice |
| Content | Section 1 of the specification | Sections 1 **and** 2 |

The two papers are sat one after the other. Questions carry equal weight, there is **no penalty for a
wrong answer**, there is **no formulae booklet**, and **calculators are not allowed**.

That works out at **3 minutes 45 seconds per question**. This is the single most important number on
this page: the questions are not individually hard for a strong A-Level student, but the direct,
grind-it-out method is almost always too slow. Paper 1 rewards spotting the shortcut — symmetry, a
substitution, a sketch, eliminating options — over correct-but-lengthy algebra.

## Scoring

One overall score on a scale from **1.0 to 9.0**, reported to one decimal place. The scale is designed
so that a typical candidate scores around **4.5**, and roughly **10% of candidates score above 7.0**.
Results come out about four weeks after the sitting.

Because there is no negative marking, **every question must be answered** — a guess on the last
question is free expected value. Budget the final minute for filling in anything left blank.

## What changed in 2024

The TMUA moved from Cambridge Assessment to **UAT-UK**, and is now taken **on screen at Pearson VUE
test centres**, with sittings in **October and January**.

The practical consequence for preparation: **question papers are no longer published.** Because the
on-screen tests reuse questions between sittings, no paper has been released since 2023. The archive
of specimen + 2016–2023 papers on this site is therefore the *complete* set of public TMUA questions,
and it is not going to grow.

The specification and the question style did not change, so the old papers remain the right practice
material. What replaced new papers is a pair of **official study guides written by the people who set
the test** — see below.

| Resource | What it is |
|---|---|
| [Content Specification](https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/03165619/TMUA_Content_Specification.pdf) | The syllabus. Section 1 = maths content (both papers), Section 2 = logic and proof (Paper 2 only) |
| [Notes on Mathematics](https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/30103537/Notes_on_Mathematics_-for_TMUA_and_ESAT_M2.pdf) | 159 pages, MM1–MM8, mapped one-to-one onto Section 1. The setters' own commentary on what each spec line means |
| [Notes on Logic and Proof](https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/25160507/Notes_on_Logic_and_Proof_June2025.pdf) | 74 pages on Section 2. Effectively the *only* textbook for Paper 2 |
| [Past papers](https://esat-tmua.ac.uk/tmua-preparation-materials/) | Specimen + 2016–2023, each with worked answers and an answer key |
| [Pearson VUE practice tests](https://www.pearsonvue.com/us/en/uatuk.html) | The on-screen interface. Sit at least one so the format is not a surprise on the day |

## How to prepare

1. **Read the specification first**, not last. It is short, and it is the contract — anything outside
   it cannot be asked.
2. **Paper 2 content before Paper 2 papers.** Logic and proof is not in the A-Level syllabus, so
   attempting Paper 2 questions cold mostly teaches frustration. Work through the
   [Paper 2 Toolkit](../toolkit/index.qmd) and the official Notes on Logic and Proof first.
3. **Papers under timed conditions.** 75 minutes, no calculator, no interruptions. An untimed TMUA
   paper measures something the real test does not.
4. **Review the questions you got right but slowly.** On this test, a two-minute overrun is as
   expensive as a wrong answer, and the worked answers usually show a faster route than the one you took.
5. **Sit a Pearson VUE practice test** before the real thing, for the interface rather than the maths.
